The numerical example of the article

Source: vignettes/claim_scoped_diagnostic_gates.Rmd
claim_scoped_diagnostic_gates.Rmd

The article illustrates Claim-Scoped Diagnostic Gates (CSDG) with two items that carry the same information. Let Z be standard normal, let both items and the outcome equal Z, and use squared error. Model A predicts with item 1, f_A(x) = x1, and model B with item 2, f_B(x) = x2. In model A, shuffling item 1 replaces the prediction Z with an independent draw Z', so the expected squared error rises from 0 to E[(Z - Z')^2] = 2; shuffling item 2 leaves the prediction unchanged, so its permutation feature importance (PFI) is 0. Model B reverses the values. Grouped PFI, which shuffles both items together, is 2 in both models; conditional PFI, which draws the permuted item given the other item, is 0, because that draw equals the original value. This vignette computes these values from 10,000 simulated observations and assesses the three claims of the article with the functions introduced in vignette("exploratory_workflow", package = "mlr3autoiml").

library(mlr3autoiml)
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3learners)
library(mlr3pipelines)

Data, models, and PFI

Each model is a linear model of one item, which reproduces the outcome exactly in every fold. The supplied strata are the exact values of Z (strata), so each stratum is one row: permuting an item within its stratum leaves it unchanged, which is the conditional distribution of one item given the other, and conditional PFI is exactly 0. The package warns about such small strata, because in real data they usually mean that the permutation changes almost nothing.

set.seed(1)
z = rnorm(10000)
task = as_task_regr(data.frame(item_1 = z, item_2 = z, y = z), target = "y", id = "numerical_example")
model_using = function(item) {
  as_learner(po("select", selector = selector_name(item), id = paste0("use_", item)) %>>% lrn("regr.lm"))
}
fits = csdg_fit(task, list(A = model_using("item_1"), B = model_using("item_2")), folds = 5,
  measure = "regr.mse", labels = c(A = "model A", B = "model B"), seed = 1)
#> Warning: package 'future' was built under R version 4.5.2
imp = csdg_importance(fits, repetitions = 20, groups = list(both_items = c("item_1", "item_2")),
  strata = list(item_1 = z, item_2 = z), seed = 2)
#> Warning: Conditional PFI of item_1 and item_2: the median stratum size in the
#> held-out folds is 1, below 5; permutation within such small strata changes few
#> values (none in strata of one row).
imp
#> <CSDGImportance> held-out PFI, increase in squared error; 5 folds x 20 permutations
#> model A: held-out squared error 0.0000 versus 1.02 for the model without predictors (improvement 1.02)
#>   predictor   mean PFI   relative to improvement   folds in top 1
#>   item_1          2.05                      200%              5/5
#>   item_2             0                      0.0%              0/5
#>   grouped: both_items (item_1, item_2) 2.05 (200%)
#>   conditional: item_1, within the supplied strata: 0 (0.0%)
#>   conditional: item_2, within the supplied strata: 0 (0.0%)
#> model B: held-out squared error 0.0000 versus 1.02 for the model without predictors (improvement 1.02)
#>   predictor   mean PFI   relative to improvement   folds in top 1
#>   item_2          2.04                      200%              5/5
#>   item_1             0                      0.0%              0/5
#>   grouped: both_items (item_1, item_2) 2.05 (200%)
#>   conditional: item_1, within the supplied strata: 0 (0.0%)
#>   conditional: item_2, within the supplied strata: 0 (0.0%)
#> Folds in top 1: folds in which the predictor has the largest PFI value (print(imp, k = )).
#> PFI values are not parts of the improvement, so PFI relative to the improvement can exceed 100%.

The estimates are close to the exact values; relative to the improvement over the model without predictors, they are about 200%, because PFI values are not parts of the improvement. The claims below are derived from these results, so the package labels their assessments exploratory.

The original claim covers both models 

items = c(item_1 = "item 1", item_2 = "item 2")
claim_both = claim_order(imp, "item_1", "item_2", learners = c("A", "B"), marginal_only = TRUE, labels = items)
res_both = csdg_assess(csdg_check(claim_both, imp))
res_both
#> <CSDG assessment> Under marginal permutation, model A and model B both rely
#> more on item 1 than on item 2.
#>   Not met (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement (G0b) supported | Procedure (G2)
#>   for model A supported | Stability (G5) for model A supported | Content (G6a)
#>   for model A supported | Minimum importance (G6a) for model A supported |
#>   Content (G6a) for model B contradicted | Minimum importance (G6a) for model B
#>   contradicted
#>   Content (G6a) for model B is contradicted: on average, item 1 0 versus item 2
#>   2.04 (difference -2.04 [-2.14, -1.95]); criterion: a positive difference;
#>   also, minimum importance (G6a) for model B is contradicted: item 1 has 0.0%
#>   of the improvement, below the minimum of 1% (0.0102). Revise the claim to
#>   what the evidence supports, or withhold it; where the claim matters, report
#>   it as not supported.
#>   Decision options: revise or withhold

The claim is not met (exploratory): it covers both models, so its content is checked for each under G6a, and model B reverses the ordering.

The qualifier is needed

On realistic inputs, where the items are equal, A and B are the same function; only a permuted input has unequal items. Without the qualifier “under marginal permutation,” the claim about model A states more than marginal PFI shows.

claim_a = claim_order(imp, "item_1", "item_2", learners = "A", labels = items)
res_a = csdg_assess(csdg_check(claim_a, imp))
res_a
#> <CSDG assessment> Model A relies more on item 1 than on item 2.
#>   Not met (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement (G0b) supported | Content (G2)
#>   supported | Minimum importance (G2) supported | Procedure (G2) contradicted |
#>   Stability (G5) supported
#>   Procedure (G2) is contradicted: within the supplied strata, item 1 adds 0
#>   (below the minimum importance 0.0102); the order is supported only under
#>   marginal permutation. Revise the claim to what the evidence supports, or
#>   withhold it; where the claim matters, report it as not supported.
#>   Options on these results (exploratory; check before reporting): marginal_only
#>   = TRUE limits the wording to marginal permutation.
#>   Decision options: revise or withhold

Conditional PFI is 0 for both items, so the procedure property (G2) is contradicted and the claim is not met (exploratory).

The revised claim

The revised claim names model A and the marginal permutation.

claim_revised = claim_order(imp, "item_1", "item_2", learners = "A", marginal_only = TRUE, labels = items)
chk_revised = csdg_check(claim_revised, imp)
chk_revised
#> <CSDG check> Under marginal permutation, model A relies more on item 1 than on
#> item 2.
#> Criteria (defaults, see ?csdg_check): minimum importance 1% of the improvement;
#> at least 5 of 5 folds; Monte Carlo rule; corrected 95% interval must clear the
#> smallest relevant difference.
#> gate  check               status        observation
#> G0a/b scope               supported     The six scope elements are generated
#>                                         from the analysis; the claim names
#>                                         analyzed variables, not constructs.
#> G1    performance         context       Held-out squared error 0.0000 versus
#>                                         1.02 for the model without predictors
#>                                         (improvement 1.02, 100%); 5 of 5 folds
#>                                         improve.
#> G2    content             supported     item 1 2.05 versus item 2 0; difference
#>                                         (PFI of item 1 minus PFI of item 2)
#>                                         2.05 [1.96, 2.14].
#> G2    minimum importance  supported     item 1 2.05 (200%) of the improvement
#>                                         of 1.02 (1.02 to 0.0000).
#> G2    procedure           supported     Held-out marginal PFI with squared
#>                                         error, 20 permutations per fold in 5
#>                                         folds, as the scope names. Conditional
#>                                         PFI of item 1 and item 2 is 0 and 0
#>                                         (the order is not established, within
#>                                         Monte Carlo error); within the supplied
#>                                         strata, item 1 adds 0 (below the
#>                                         minimum importance 0.0102). The wording
#>                                         names the marginal permutation, so the
#>                                         reversal shows what the qualifier is
#>                                         for. Grouped PFI of both_items (item_1,
#>                                         item_2) 2.05 measures reliance on the
#>                                         group; it does not order its members.
#> G5    stability           supported     item 1 exceeds item 2 in 5 of 5 folds.
#> G6a   other learner       context       model B: the result does not hold (item
#>                                         1 0 versus item 2 2.04).
res_revised = csdg_assess(chk_revised)
res_revised
#> <CSDG assessment> Under marginal permutation, model A relies more on item 1
#> than on item 2.
#>   Met (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement (G0b) supported | Content (G2)
#>   supported | Minimum importance (G2) supported | Procedure (G2) supported |
#>   Stability (G5) supported
#>   On average, item 1 2.05 versus item 2 0 (difference 2.05 [1.96, 2.14]); item
#>   1 exceeds item 2 in 5 of 5 folds. The claim was formulated after the
#>   explanation was inspected; it is established only after a test on new data
#>   (csdg_confirm()).
#>   Decision options: retain

The revised claim is met (exploratory). Model B’s reversal is context, because the claim no longer covers model B, and the grouped PFI measures reliance on the pair rather than ordering its members.

Further reading

In the article’s variant with items of different reliability, the model that uses the more reliable item has the larger PFI, although both items measure the same Z; importance can then reflect the reliability of a measure rather than the relevance of its construct. Analysts who record claims, scopes, and evidence by hand, for example for a claim stated before the analysis, find the record functions in ?csdg_claim, ?csdg_evidence_record, ?csdg_adjudicate_claim, and ?csdg_claim_relation.
